caption:
This year’s High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development takes place at a pivotal moment for the 2030 Agenda.
 
While energy is one of the most powerful enablers across the development agenda, 666 million people still lack access to electricity, and 2.1 billion rely on polluting fuels for cooking. These aren’t just energy issues; they're development emergencies

This week, as members of the SDG 7 Technical Advisory Group, we are launching a series of new Policy Briefs to support the HLPF discussions. They highlight just how central clean and inclusive energy is to unlocking progress across the development goals:

🌐 Zero Hunger: Energy powers irrigation, food storage and processing; critical to ending hunger and food insecurity.

🏥 Good Health and Well-being: Reliable energy keeps clinics running, vaccines cold, and clean air possible in homes and schools.

🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Gender Equality: Access to modern energy frees up time, reduces health risks and creates opportunities; especially for women and girls.

🛠️ Decent Work and Economic Growth: Energy access enables businesses to grow, jobs to be created and economies to thrive.

🏝️ Equity in LDCs, LLDCs, and SIDS: Clean energy drives local development, builds resilience and reduces dependency on volatile fuel imports.

The message is clear: energy action is development action. Without urgent investment and collaboration, we risk leaving millions behind. 

As #HLPF2025 discussions unfold, let’s turn these insights into action. Let’s scale up solutions that put energy at the heart of sustainable development for everyone, everywhere.
